# 1045 of the 1047 harvested fixtures pass, and the two left both name an IntelliJ action. There is
# nothing on this list any more that this host could do and has not.
#
# The ten that left it most recently are worth telling apart, because only eight were bugs here.
#
# Eight were blockwise Visual, and one bug: a block's caret goes in the *active corner's* column
# rather than the block's right edge, a line too short to hold the block's slice contributes no
# caret at all, carets that have stopped being different carets merge, and two pieces of per-caret
# state have to outlive the caret that recorded them. `VsCodeBlockVisualTest` has the numbers.
#
# One was the harness harvesting tests IdeaVim has `@Disabled`. `search in one time from select
# mode` sat here as "expected [81], actual [82]" when IdeaVim's own caret is at 82, and `repeat
# command with execution of ij action` had a reason written against it - a missing IntelliJ action -
# that was not why it failed. A disabled test does not pass over there either. Before believing an
# entry in this file, check that the fixture passes in the plugin.
#
# And one was `'incsearch'` previewing an ex command, which this port had recorded as needing "a
# different piece of machinery from previewing `/`". True, and the machinery already existed: it was
# `parseCommandLineForPreview` in `ExEntryPanel`, in `src/main/java` next to a Swing document
# listener, with no IntelliJ in the body of it. It is `incsearchPreviewRequest` in the engine now
# and both hosts read it.

# --- Two IntelliJ actions, which this host has no equivalent of.
#
# `ideajoin` is IntelliJ's smart join, a language feature this host cannot have: `VjJ` with the
# option set joins the way the language wants rather than the way Vim does.
#
# `partial Action mapping` types `X(EditorToggleCase)` into a half-declared `<Action>` mapping. The
# mapping machinery works - nothing is inserted as literal text, which is what this entry used to
# claim - and `EditorToggleCase` is an IntelliJ action id with no VS Code command behind it. There
# is no toggle-case command; `editor.action.transformToUppercase` and its lowercase twin are the
# whole of what VS Code offers.
